meta.description: Every parameter used by the Crew Health model (app.ml), with its source and status. Loaded by app.ml.params; do not hardcode these values elsewhere.

status_definitions.literature: value stated directly in the cited source (read by us)
status_definitions.derived: computed from literature values with the formula given in 'note'
status_definitions.assumed: no accessible source; modelling assumption, must be disclosed

NASA_JSC_2005_REQ.citation: NASA JSC Nutritional Biochemistry Laboratory. Nutrition Requirements, Standards, and Operating Bands for Exploration Missions. Initial Release (rev 1), Dec 2005. NTRS 20200001703 (JSC-E-DAA-TN71711).

COOPER_2017.citation: Cooper M, Perchonok M, Douglas GL. Initial assessment of the nutritional quality of the space food system over three years of ambient storage. npj Microgravity 3:17 (2017).

GOULETTE_2020.citation: Goulette TR, Zhou J, Dixon WR, Normand MD, Peleg M, McClements DJ, Decker E, Xiao H. Kinetic parameters of thiamine degradation in NASA spaceflight foods determined by the endpoints method for long-term storage. Food Chemistry 302:125365 (2020; online 2019).
GOULETTE_2020.access: abstract only (Europe PMC); full text paywalled, kinetic parameters (rate constants, temperature sensitivity) NOT accessed

SMITH_2005.citation: Smith SM, Zwart SR, Block G, Rice BL, Davis-Street JE. The nutritional status of astronauts is altered after long-term space flight aboard the International Space Station. J Nutr 135(3):437-443 (2005).
SMITH_2005.access: abstract only (Europe PMC); full text (Elsevier) returned HTTP 403

RICE_ZWART_SMITH_NTRS.citation: Rice BL, Zwart SR, Smith SM. Vitamin D in Real and Simulated Weightlessness: Implications for Earth. Conference abstract (ADA), NASA JSC. NTRS 20080026180. Reports the same n = 11 ISS cohort as SMITH_2005.

SMITH_ZWART_NTRS_2006.citation: Smith SM, Zwart SR. Nutrition issues for space exploration. NASA JSC manuscript, NTRS 20060049121 (ISS Expeditions 1-12, n = 15).

SMITH_2009_ANTARCTIC.citation: Smith SM, Gardner KK, Locke J, Zwart SR. Vitamin D supplementation during Antarctic winter. Am J Clin Nutr 89(4):1092-1098 (2009).

MODEL_ASSUMPTION.citation: Modelling assumption of this project (no source).

parameters.name: vitamin_c.pool_max_mg
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin C, 'Body stores and relative time to depletion' (printed p. 53): 'Maximum body pools of ascorbate are ~2 grams.'
parameters.note: Upper cap of the first-order body pool.

parameters.name: vitamin_c.risk_threshold_mg
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin C (printed p. 54): 'Intake below the RDA can cause a deficiency once the body pools fall below ~300 mg of ascorbic acid.'
parameters.note: Pool level treated as the risk crossing. Early warning comes from the ACT/WATCH forecast horizon, not from raising the threshold.

parameters.name: vitamin_c.catabolic_turnover_mg_day
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin C (printed p. 53): 'Catabolic turnover varies from 10 to 45 mg/day and with low intakes, turnover is reduced.'
parameters.note: Used to derive the first-order turnover rate and in the literature check.

parameters.name: vitamin_c.turnover_per_day
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from printed p. 53 (max turnover 45 mg/day, max pool ~2000 mg).
parameters.note: k = 45 mg/day / 2000 mg = 0.0225 per day (first-order: turnover proportional to pool, consistent with 'with low intakes, turnover is reduced').

parameters.name: vitamin_c.absorption
parameters.unit: fraction (effective: absorbed and retained in the body pool)
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from Vitamin C, 'Body stores and relative time to depletion' (printed p. 53): tissue saturation at intakes of 100-140 mg/day, catabolic turnover up to 45 mg/day, maximum body pool ~2 g.
parameters.note: Steady-state calibration. First-order pool P_eq = a * I / k. Require P_eq = P_max (2000 mg) at the saturation intake I_sat = 120 mg/day (midpoint of 100-140) with k = 0.0225/day (vitamin_c.turnover_per_day): a = k * P_max / I_sat = 45 / 120 = 0.375 (0.32-0.45 across 100-140 mg/day). Anchored to the saturation intake, not the 90 mg/day requirement, because ~2 g is the MAXIMUM pool, reached at saturation. Effective efficiency (intestinal absorption x renal retention), not intestinal absorption alone: the linear model has no saturable renal-excretion term, so urinary loss of unmetabolised ascorbate is folded into a. Old 0.70 (assumed) implied saturation at 64 mg/day, below the literature range.

parameters.name: vitamin_c.requirement_mg_day
parameters.where_in_source: Req. 11 (printed p. 55): 'The dietary intake of vitamin C shall be 90 mg/day.'
parameters.note: Daily need used to size the intake gap and food recommendation.

parameters.name: vitamin_c.scurvy_onset_days
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin C (printed p. 54): 'Scurvy is seen in adults within 45 to 80 days of stopping vitamin C intake.'
parameters.note: Literature check only (time from full pool to deficiency pool at zero intake).

parameters.name: vitamin_c.saturation_intake_mg_day
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin C (printed p. 53): 'Blood cell and tissue concentrations become saturated at intakes from 100 to 140 mg/day'.
parameters.note: Calibration anchor for vitamin_c.absorption (midpoint 120 mg/day). The literature check of the saturating intake is therefore a calibration identity.

parameters.name: thiamine_b1.pool_max_mg
parameters.where_in_source: Thiamin, 'Body stores and relative time to depletion' (printed p. 60): 'Approximately 30 mg of thiamin is stored in the human body'.
parameters.note: Old value happened to match the literature.

parameters.name: thiamine_b1.half_life_days
parameters.where_in_source: Thiamin (printed p. 60): 'The biological half-life of thiamin is in the range of 9 to 18 days.'
parameters.note: Upper bound (18 d) used to derive turnover_per_day (see its note: the only part of the range consistent with the 30 mg store at 1.2 mg/day and absorption <= 1); range used in the literature check.

parameters.name: thiamine_b1.turnover_per_day
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from printed p. 60 (half-life 9-18 days; ~30 mg body store; RDA 1.2 mg/day for men).
parameters.note: k = ln 2 / 18 days (upper end of the 9-18 day half-life range). Chosen jointly with thiamine_b1.absorption: the steady-state store anchor (30 mg at 1.2 mg/day) needs a = 30 k / 1.2 <= 1, i.e. t1/2 >= 30 ln2 / 1.2 = 17.3 days. The previous midpoint 13.5 days (k = 0.0513/day) would need a = 1.28, physically impossible, so the three literature anchors are only mutually consistent for t1/2 in [17.3, 18] days; 18 days is the literature-stated bound inside that interval.

parameters.name: thiamine_b1.risk_threshold_fraction_of_store
parameters.note: Risk crossing at 1/3 of the ~30 mg body store (= 10 mg, unchanged value). Searched NASA_JSC_2005_REQ thiamin section (printed pp. 60-61) and SMITH_ZWART_NTRS_2006 (no thiamin content): neither states a body-pool level or a depletion time at which deficiency signs appear. NASA assesses thiamin status by erythrocyte transketolase activation (green 0%, yellow 15%, red >25%) and sets intake bands (Req. 14, men: green 1.2, yellow 0.8-1.0, red <0.8 per day). Not used: the red intake edge maps to a steady-state pool of 30 * 0.8 / 1.2 = 20 mg in this model, but it is an intake band, not a level at which deficiency signs appear.

parameters.name: thiamine_b1.absorption
parameters.unit: fraction (effective: absorbed and retained in the body pool)
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from Thiamin (printed p. 60): 'Approximately 30 mg of thiamin is stored in the human body', half-life 9-18 days; RDA 1.2 mg/day for men.
parameters.note: Steady-state calibration: a = P_store * k / I_RDA = 30 mg * (ln2 / 18 d) / 1.2 mg/day = 0.963. Assumes the ~30 mg store is the steady state of an adult eating the RDA (the source does not state the intake behind the 30 mg figure). Old 0.60 (assumed) gave a 14 mg steady state at the RDA.

parameters.name: thiamine_b1.requirement_mg_day
parameters.where_in_source: Thiamin, 'Nominal requirement on Earth' (printed p. 60): 'The thiamin RDA is 1.2 mg/day for men aged 19 and older and 1.1 mg/day for women'; Req. 14 (printed p. 61).
parameters.note: Req. 14 prints the unit as 'umol/day', apparently a typo for mg/day given the RDA text. Men's value used for the whole (synthetic, unsexed) crew.

parameters.name: kinetics.thiamine_b1.reference
parameters.where_in_source: Abstract: model-predicted thiamine retention at 20 C for 720 days: brown rice 55%, split pea soup 42%, beef brisket 3%.
parameters.note: grain = brown rice, legume = split pea soup, meat = BBQ beef brisket (all NASA thermostabilized foods).

parameters.name: kinetics.thiamine_b1.k_ref_per_day
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from abstract endpoints.
parameters.note: First-order k_ref = -ln(retention) / 720 days.

parameters.name: kinetics.vitamin_c.reference
parameters.where_in_source: Results / Fig. 2: 'The vitamin C content in most fruit products degraded between 32 and 83% after 3 years of storage'; Methods: stored at 21 C.
parameters.note: Measured on fruit products only; Cooper notes vitamin C stability depends on food matrix.

parameters.name: kinetics.vitamin_c.k_ref_per_day
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from Results / Fig. 2 range.
parameters.note: Midpoint loss 57.5% -> retention 0.425; k_ref = -ln(0.425) / 1095 days. Applied to every packaged menu item (matrix-specific values not available).

parameters.name: kinetics.activation_energy
parameters.value: per-item activation_energy_Ea_kJ_mol from space_food_catalog.json (40-45 kJ/mol for menu items)
parameters.note: TODO: temperature sensitivity for thiamine is in Goulette 2020 full text (not accessed); none found for vitamin C in space foods. Only used to scale k_ref away from 20-21 C; catalog per-item A factors are no longer used by the crew model.

parameters.name: kinetics.food_class_map
parameters.note: Beef fajitas, shrimp, salmon -> meat (Cooper 2017 Fig. 3 also reports B1 less stable in animal products); oatmeal -> grain; lentil stew -> legume (split pea soup); macadamia/cranberry -> grain (no nut data).

parameters.name: vitamin_d.preflight_25ohd_nmol_l
parameters.where_in_source: Text: 'serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol was 25% less after landing (48 +/- 20) than before flight (63 +/- 16) (P < 0.01)', n = 11 ISS crew.
parameters.note: Each synthetic astronaut's pre-flight level is drawn from N(63, 16).

parameters.name: vitamin_d.postflight_25ohd_nmol_l
parameters.where_in_source: Same sentence as preflight value.
parameters.note: SMITH_2005 abstract (same cohort) confirms direction and significance: 'Despite vitamin D supplement use during flight, serum 25-hydroxycholecalciferol was decreased after flight (P < 0.01).'

parameters.name: vitamin_d.iss_mission_days
parameters.where_in_source: Abstract: '11 astronauts before and after long-duration (128-195 d) space flight'.
parameters.note: Midpoint 161.5 days used to convert the pre/post change to a rate.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.supplement_ug_day
parameters.where_in_source: Text: 'Crewmembers (n = 11) were provided vitamin D supplements (as cholecalciferol (10 ug/d) throughout the mission.'
parameters.note: Also 400 IU/day in SMITH_ZWART_NTRS_2006 Methods 2.2.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.supplement_doses_per_week
parameters.where_in_source: Text: 'The average number of vitamin D supplements reported to be consumed per week was 5.7 +/- 4.0.'
parameters.note: Per-astronaut compliance drawn from N(5.7, 4.0) clipped to [0, 7], divided by 7.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.decline_rate_per_day_iss
parameters.where_in_source: Derived from 63 -> 48 nmol/L over the 128-195 d missions (SMITH_2005).
parameters.note: r = ln(63/48) / 161.5 days, i.e. the decline under ISS supplementation (10 ug x 5.7/7 = 8.14 ug/day mean). Extrapolating it beyond 195 days (Mars 450 Sols = 462 days) is an assumption.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.requirement_ug_day
parameters.where_in_source: Req. 8 (printed p. 45): 'The dietary intake of vitamin D shall be 25 ug per day.' (green band 25-50 ug/d)
parameters.note: Target intake used for recommendations.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.food_intake_ug_day
parameters.note: TODO: space_food_catalog.json has no vitamin D field. Cooper 2017 Results: vitamin D in the food system was 'not adequate to meet recommended nutrient daily intake' and 'Vitamin D is generally low in food' (no number given). Conservative 0.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.intake_response
parameters.value: decline_rate = r_iss * max(0, requirement - intake) / (requirement - iss_intake)
parameters.note: Linear interpolation between two literature anchors: ISS intake (8.14 ug/day) gives the measured decline; NASA Req. 8 intake (25 ug/day) is treated as status-maintaining. No in-flight dose-response study was accessible. No UV synthesis term (spacecraft shielded; SMITH_ZWART_NTRS_2006 Background).

parameters.name: vitamin_d.risk_threshold_nmol_l
parameters.where_in_source: Req. 8 standards (printed p. 45): '25-Hydroxy Vitamin D ... 25-138 nmol/L green'; SMITH_ZWART_NTRS_2006 Discussion: 'deficiency at < 25 nmol 25-hydroxyvitamin D/L'.
parameters.note: Lower edge of NASA green band. Both sources note many experts argue 80 nmol/L should be normal (vitamin_d.optimal_nmol_l).

parameters.name: vitamin_d.optimal_nmol_l
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin D (printed p. 43): 'optimal serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D may be as high as 80 nmol/L'; also SMITH_2009_ANTARCTIC abstract.
parameters.note: Reported for context in the API; not used as the risk threshold.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.iu_per_ug
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin D (printed p. 43): '(25 ug or 1000 IU)'.
parameters.note: Unit conversion for recommendations.

parameters.name: vitamin_d.mir_decline_pct
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin D (printed p. 43): Mir crew 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 '32%-36% less during and after long-duration (3- to 4-month) missions'.
parameters.note: Literature check only (Mir supplementation not stated; months converted at 30 days).

parameters.name: vitamin_d.short_mission_no_decline_days
parameters.where_in_source: Vitamin D (printed p. 44): 'vitamin D status was decreased after long missions (84 to 195 d), but not after shorter missions (28 to 59 d)'.
parameters.note: Literature check only: model decline at 59 days should be smaller than the pre-flight between-subject SD (16 nmol/L).

parameters.name: vitamin_d.antarctic_no_uv_5mo_nmol_l
parameters.where_in_source: Abstract, Results.
parameters.note: Reference only (baseline values not in abstract, so not used in the model). Supports recommending 1000-2000 IU/day when UV is absent.

parameters.name: crew.appetite_fraction
parameters.note: Range assumed; its mean (0.80) matches SMITH_2005 abstract 'Crew members consumed a mean of 80% of their recommended energy intake' (checked in literature_check).

parameters.name: crew.energy_intake_fraction_iss
parameters.where_in_source: Abstract: 'Crew members consumed a mean of 80% of their recommended energy intake'.
parameters.note: Literature check only. SMITH_ZWART_NTRS_2006 Results report 74 +/- 11% of WHO recommendation for n = 15.

parameters.name: crew.turnover_scale
parameters.note: TODO: individual variation in vitamin turnover; no source.

parameters.name: crew.intake_daily_noise_sd
parameters.note: Day-to-day intake variability.

parameters.name: crew.vitals_profile
parameters.note: Synthetic personal baselines for observable vitals.

parameters.name: crew.vitals_deficit_mapping
parameters.note: Demonstration-only mapping from vitamin C / B1 deficit signal to vitals. No clinical meaning.

parameters.name: crew.vitals_noise
parameters.note: Measurement / day-to-day noise of synthetic vitals; body mass noise is AR(1) mean-reverting.

parameters.name: scenario.post_event_response
parameters.note: Scenario design: switch to survival rations, stress-related appetite drop, greenhouse loss after the cooling/power event.
